heroHeadline: Day 769: Search-Collective Founder Alma Rosa Rojo Medina Shot in Culiacán; Chapitos Financial Operator Detained in Mexicali; Army Blankets Schools Statewide for New Year
heroSubtitle: 769 days of cartel civil war — through August 31, 2026: Gunmen shot search-collective founder Alma Rosa Rojo Medina and her daughter in Culiacán's Estela Ortiz de Toledo neighborhood on August 29 — the second attack against Rojo Medina, whose 'Voces Unidas por la Vida' collective has lost members to cartel violence twice already in 2026; state prosecutors opened an attempted-femicide investigation. The same week, a binational operation involving Mexican security forces, the DEA and US Treasury OFAC detained Salvador 'El Chava' Díaz Rodríguez, an alleged Chapitos money launderer accused of laundering over $50 million, in Mexicali on August 27. Statewide security operations across all 20 municipalities during the week of August 23–30 yielded 16 detentions, 40 explosive devices and dozens of firearms. As Sinaloa opened its 2026–2027 school year on August 31, the Army and state police deployed to schools statewide after unknown gunmen left a funeral wreath and threatening graffiti outside a private school in Culiacán overnight — part of interim Governor Graciela Domínguez Nava's continuing federal-backed 'Plan Integral de Seguridad y Gobernabilidad,' announced days after her August 25 swearing-in. Statewide violence continues unabated: July 2026 closed as the deadliest month of the year for women (12 femicide investigations, later revised to 71 femicides accumulated for 2026 as of Aug 27) and the second-deadliest overall (138 violent deaths), while La Mayiza continues to hold roughly 90% territorial control under a four-faction fragmented cartel structure (International Crisis Group, July 7).
